id: I-0372
provider: local
kind: issue
body: 'DECISION NEEDED: the rational-point hypothesis, and the blueprint describing
  an abandoned route.


  Two things surfaced by an adversarially-verified six-front assessment on 2026-07-27
  that only you can settle. Both outrank every mechanical improvement in flight.


  1. THE RATIONAL POINT. references/challenge.lean declares ''Jacobian C'' with NO
  rational-point binder. But instHasPicScheme (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316)
  makes ''[HasRationalPoint C]'' an ESSENTIAL hypothesis, and correctly so -- without
  a section, Pic(C x_k T) / pi_T^* Pic(T) need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman''s
  theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed
  to be a platform limitation; it is not. Mathlib v4.31 does carry the etale topology
  (.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50). So it
  is a design choice, and as the tree stands the project would prove something strictly
  weaker than the challenge asks. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept
  the weaker theorem and say so. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until
  it is settled. Roadmap node AJC.picrep.rational-point.


  2. THE BLUEPRINT ADVERTISES A ROUTE THE TREE ABANDONED. informal/pic-representability-campaign.md
  (2026-07-09) selected route D3 Milne-Kollar -- section trick on the Div substrate,
  finite Galois quotient, coproduct assembly -- and states verbatim ''Off-path and
  untouched: Quot-lane sorries''. FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550 marks HasSmoothProperQuotient
  ''PERMANENTLY OFF-PATH ... Do not build new consumers against it'', and Scheme.QuotScheme
  has ZERO consumers. Meanwhile Picard_QuotScheme.tex is 8,434 lines and roadmap nodes
  AJC.picrep.quot / .serre / .assembly still describe it as the strategy. The sunk
  cost is small -- only QuotRepresentability.lean (83 lines) and SerreFiniteness.lean
  (292) are exclusive to the Quot endgame; the other ~9k lines are imported by the
  committed route and must NOT be deleted. Decide: re-aim the blueprint and roadmap
  at the Milne-Kollar route actually being built, or deliberately revive Quot.


  CONTEXT FOR THE DECISION. Representability is months away, not weeks: 18 of the
  campaign''s 28 milestones have zero Lean written (verified by file absence), including
  all of cluster J, the actual Milne construction of Pic^r. Estimate 27k-45k new lines,
  i.e. 22-37% again of the current 121k-line tree; 1-3 months at staffed throughput.
  The single gate is HasRigidPushforward (B3) -- seven direct dependents, and the
  only route in the tree from a line bundle to a DivFamily; it is reduced to ''GeometricallyIntegral
  (p1Over k).hom'', a bounded ~200-350 LOC brick, plus the hfib bridge. The longest
  pole is cluster P (Riemann-Roch chi-ledger, section drops, uniform H^1 vanishing),
  which has ZERO lines in AJC -- but the sibling AJCR has a sorry-free 17,792-line,
  62-module RiemannRoch/ directory that is essentially cluster P. A day auditing AJCR
  for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof
  would.


  ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the headline is unwired. Jacobian.lean imports only AlgebraicJacobian.Genus,
  so none of the 122k lines of Picard/Albanese/Cohomology work is reachable from picardJacobianWitness.
  And two sorry-bodied INSTANCES leak through typeclass synthesis -- instHasPicScheme
  (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:317, sole producer, 41 use sites) and pullback_preservesFiniteLimits
  (CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:163) -- so ''153 sorry-free modules'' is
  a LOCAL claim, not an axiom-cleanliness claim. Run ''#print axioms'' on the headline
  declarations before believing any completeness number.'

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Genus
8	
9	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
10	
11	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
12	its structure as an abelian variety.
13	
14	## Status
15	
16	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
17	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
18	project from the witness directly.
19	
20	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
21	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
22	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
23	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
24	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
25	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
26	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
27	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
28	
29	This file contains exactly ONE `sorry`-bodied mathematical declaration,
30	`picardJacobianWitness`, whose closure is the FGA construction of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` as an
31	abelian variety with its Albanese universal property.
32	
33	The file contains:
34	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
35	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
36	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
37	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
38	- `picardJacobianWitness`: the Albanese witness `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}`, body `sorry`.
39	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
40	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
41	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
42	  Albanese witness.
43	
44	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
45	
46	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
47	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
48	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
49	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
50	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
51	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
52	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
53	-/
54	
55	set_option autoImplicit false
56	
57	universe u
58	
59	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
60	
61	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
62	
63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
64	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
65	  [IsProper C.hom]
66	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
67	
68	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
69	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
70	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
71	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
72	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
73	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
74	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
75	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
76	      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
77	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g
78	
79	namespace IsAlbanese
80	
81	noncomputable def ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
82	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
83	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
84	  Classical.choose h
85	
86	lemma comp_ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
87	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
88	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
89	    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=
90	  (Classical.choose_spec h).1
91	
92	lemma exists_unique_ofCurve_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
93	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
94	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J)
95	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
96	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
97	    ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = h.ofCurve ≫ g :=
98	  (Classical.choose_spec h).2 f hf
99	
100	/-- The Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the
101	universal morphisms. -/
102	theorem unique {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C}
103	    {J₁ J₂ : Over (Spec (.of k))}
104	    [GrpObj J₁] [IsProper J₁.hom] [Smooth J₁.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₁.hom]
105	    [GrpObj J₂] [IsProper J₂.hom] [Smooth J₂.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₂.hom]
106	    (h₁ : IsAlbanese C P J₁) (h₂ : IsAlbanese C P J₂) :
107	    ∃! (e : J₁ ⟶ J₂), h₂.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ e := by
108	  have ⟨g, hg_eq, hg_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
109	  have ⟨h, hh_eq, hh_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
110	  have ⟨g₁, hg₁_eq, hg₁_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
111	  have g₁_eq_id : g₁ = 𝟙 J₁ := by
112	    refine (hg₁_unique (𝟙 J₁) ?_).symm
113	    simp
114	  have ggh_eq_g₁ : g ≫ h = g₁ := by
115	    refine hg₁_unique (g ≫ h) ?_
116	    change h₁.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ (g ≫ h)
117	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hg_eq, ← hh_eq]
118	  have hgh : g ≫ h = 𝟙 J₁ := by rw [ggh_eq_g₁, g₁_eq_id]
119	  have ⟨k₂, hk₂_eq, hk₂_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
120	  have k₂_eq_id : k₂ = 𝟙 J₂ := by
121	    refine (hk₂_unique (𝟙 J₂) ?_).symm
122	    simp
123	  have hhg_eq_k₂ : h ≫ g = k₂ := by
124	    refine hk₂_unique (h ≫ g) ?_
125	    change h₂.ofCurve = h₂.ofCurve ≫ (h ≫ g)
126	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hh_eq, ← hg_eq]
127	  have hhg : h ≫ g = 𝟙 J₂ := by rw [hhg_eq_k₂, k₂_eq_id]
128	  exact ⟨g, hg_eq, fun g' hg' => hg_unique g' hg'⟩
129	
130	end IsAlbanese
131	
132	/-- A bundled Albanese witness for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve
133	`C`: a candidate group scheme `J` (with proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
134	structure, smooth of relative dimension `genus C`), and a proof that `J` satisfies
135	the Albanese universal property of Definition `IsAlbanese` for `C` *for every choice
136	of $k$-rational marked point* `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`.
137	
138	Mathematically, the underlying scheme `J` (and its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
139	structure) is intrinsic to `C`; only the universal morphism `C ⟶ J` depends on the
140	choice of marked point `P`. Encoding `isAlbaneseFor` as a `∀ P, IsAlbanese …` field
141	keeps the bundle independent of any specific pointing, which is what
142	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve P` needs in order to project the Albanese morphism for
143	an *arbitrary* input `P`.
144	
145	The smoothness witness is recorded at the specific relative dimension `genus C`,
146	which is the form required by `Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`. -/
147	structure JacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
148	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
149	  /-- The candidate Albanese object. -/
150	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
151	  /-- The group-scheme structure on `J`. -/
152	  grpObj : GrpObj J
153	  /-- `J` is proper over `k`. -/
154	  proper : IsProper J.hom
155	  /-- `J` is smooth over `k`. -/
156	  smooth : Smooth J.hom
157	  /-- `J` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
158	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom
159	  /-- `J` is smooth of relative dimension `genus C` (so dim `J = genus C`). -/
160	  smoothGenus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) J.hom
161	  /-- The Albanese universal-property data: for every choice of $k$-rational marked
162	  point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`, the scheme `J` together with its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
163	  structure satisfies the Albanese universal property for the pointed curve `(C, P)`. -/
164	  isAlbaneseFor : ∀ (P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C), @IsAlbanese k _ C P J grpObj proper smooth geomIrred
165	
166	
167	/-- The Albanese witness for a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C`,
168	constructed **uniformly in the genus** as the identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the
169	Picard scheme of `C`.
170	
171	By the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*`), `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is representable
172	(`Scheme.PicScheme.representable`) and is an abelian variety of dimension `genus C`:
173	its tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`),
174	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
175	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
176	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
177	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
178	
179	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
180	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
181	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
182	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
183	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke
184	rigidity / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery — has been
185	removed in favour of this single uniform witness. -/
186	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
187	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
188	    JacobianWitness C :=
189	  sorry
190	
191	/-- Existence of an Albanese witness for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible
192	curve, uniformly in the genus via the Picard identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
193	(`picardJacobianWitness`). This packages all five protected sorries (`Jacobian`,
194	`instGrpObj`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`, `instIsProper`,
195	`instGeometricallyIrreducible`) into a single existence statement, and records that the
196	Albanese property of the underlying scheme `J` is uniform over every choice of
197	`k`-rational marked point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C` (via the `isAlbaneseFor` field of
198	`JacobianWitness`). -/
199	theorem nonempty_jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
200	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
201	    Nonempty (JacobianWitness C) :=
202	  ⟨picardJacobianWitness C⟩
203	
204	/-- A choice of Albanese witness for `C`, extracted via `Classical.choice`.
205	Used to define `Jacobian C` and to discharge each of the four protected instances
206	on it. -/
207	noncomputable def jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
208	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
209	    JacobianWitness C :=
210	  Classical.choice (nonempty_jacobianWitness C)
211	
212	-- data
213	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`.
214	
215	The Jacobian is the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness for `C` (see
216	`JacobianWitness` and `nonempty_jacobianWitness`); the existence of such a
217	witness (`picardJacobianWitness`, `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}`) is the single open
218	mathematical sorry, closed by the FGA construction. The genus-`0`
219	specialisation is implicit in the witness — a smooth proper geometrically
220	irreducible group scheme over `k` of relative dimension `0` is `Spec k` — so
221	no separate genus-`0` construction is needed. -/
222	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
223	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
224	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
225	  (jacobianWitness C).J
226	
227	namespace Jacobian
228	
229	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
230	
231	-- data
232	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
233	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
234	
235	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
236	genus of `C`. -/
237	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
238	  (jacobianWitness C).smoothGenus
239	
240	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
241	instance instIsProper : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom := (jacobianWitness C).proper
242	
243	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
244	instance instGeometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
245	  (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
246	
247	end Jacobian
248	
249	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it through the
6	Grassmannian/Quot/flattening-stratification machinery, identify its identity
7	component as an abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese
8	universal property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; the
9	representability leg is the open frontier.
10	
11	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
12	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
13	
14	## State (measured 2026-07-27)
15	
16	- **164 modules, 121,662 lines.**  Exactly **24 `sorry`** remain, spread over 11
17	  modules; the other **153 modules are sorry-free**.
18	- A warm `lake build` is **green**: 8,723 jobs, and 162 warning heads across 28
19	  files, of which 24 are `declaration uses sorry`.
20	- **86 of the 164 modules still open with a bare `import Mathlib`**, and 132 of the
21	  164 inherit one transitively.  This is the dominant build cost; it is being
22	  converted bottom-up from the import-DAG sources using the helpers in `scripts/`.
23	
24	Cones closed: `AJC.substrate`, `AJC.linebundle`, `AJC.grquot`, `AJC.cech`.
25	Cones open: `AJC.fbc` (flat base change, three leaves), `AJC.rr`, `AJC.picrep`
26	(Picard representability), `AJC.pic0av` (Pic⁰ is an abelian variety),
27	`AJC.albanese`.  Run `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.jacobian` for the live tree
28	— the roadmap, not this file, is the authority on status.
29	
30	## Navigation
31	
32	- [`AlgebraicJacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian.lean): project import root.
33	- [`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean): the final
34	  Jacobian witness interface and assembly point.
35	- [`blueprint/web/index.html`](blueprint/web/index.html): generated mathematical blueprint.
36	- [`analogies/README.md`](analogies/README.md): index to the historical design notes.
37	- [`../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md):
38	  the alternative Rebuild route.
39	
40	## Layout
41	
42	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/`: sheaf cohomology, the finite-cover Čech
43	  complex, higher direct images, and flat base change.
44	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/`: line bundles, relative Spec, the relative Picard
45	  functor, Grassmannians, Quot schemes, flattening stratification, and Picard
46	  identity components.
47	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/`: rigidity and extension of rational maps, plus the
48	  Albanese factorization.
49	- `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/`: divisor and adelic Riemann–Roch infrastructure.
50	- `blueprint/src/chapters/`: the mathematical blueprint.
51	- `hgraph/`: the generated statement/declaration dependency graph.
52	- `scripts/`: import-minimization and budget-trimming helpers (`min-imports.sh`,
53	  `deumbrella.sh`, `deumbrella-wave.sh`, `trim-budgets.sh`).  They drive
54	  `lake env lean`, never `lake build`, so they do not invalidate the build tree.
55	- `informal/`, `memory/`, `analogies/`: campaign plans, durable notes, and
56	  historical design notes.  See each directory's own index.
57	- [`../../references/summary.md`](../../references/summary.md): shared source
58	  bibliography and retrieval notes.
59	
60	## Build
61	
62	Lean and Mathlib are both pinned at `v4.31.0`.
63	
64	```bash
65	lake exe cache get
66	lake build
67	```
68	
69	For faithful checks, prefer the configured module target.  `lake env lean <file>`
70	does not apply every option from the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` — in particular
71	`maxSynthPendingDepth` — so a direct-file-only instance-synthesis failure can be an
72	option mismatch rather than a source regression.  Files that rely on that option
73	carry a local `set_option` so direct-file, LSP, and module checks agree.
74	
75	This project is part of an Archon Horizon workspace.  Roadmap, task, inbox, and
76	cross-project state live at the workspace root and are reached through the
77	`horizon` CLI.

1	---
2	name: blueprint-conventions
3	description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
4	---
5	
6	Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
7	Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.
8	
9	## Environments
10	
11	Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
12	`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
13	`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
14	its following `proof` environment form one node's content.
15	
16	## Per-node macros
17	
18	- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
19	- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
20	  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
21	  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
22	  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
23	  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
24	- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
25	  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
26	  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
27	  proof.
28	- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
29	  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
30	  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
31	- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
32	  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
33	  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
34	- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
35	  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
36	
37	## House style
38	
39	- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
40	  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
41	  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
42	  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
43	  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
44	  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
45	  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
46	  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
47	- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
48	  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
49	  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
50	  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
51	  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
52	  its proof stays complete.
53	- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
54	  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
55	- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
56	  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
57	  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
58	  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

/-- **Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`.**

For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, the identity component
`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k` (Kleiman §5 Thm.~`th:qpp&p`; a smooth proper
curve is geometrically normal, hence the projectivity upgrade applies).

The proof (iter-194+): `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is quasi-projective (Kleiman §5
Thm.~`th:qpp&p`, first conclusion); to upgrade to projective (hence proper)
we use the Chevalley–Rosenlicht structure theorem to reduce to ruling out
non-constant `k̄`-morphisms `𝔾_m → Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. The latter follows from

10	
11	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
12	its structure as an abelian variety.
13	
14	## Status
15	
16	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
17	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
18	project from the witness directly.
19	
20	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
21	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
22	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
23	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
24	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
25	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
26	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
27	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
28	
29	This file contains exactly ONE `sorry`-bodied mathematical declaration,
30	`picardJacobianWitness`, whose closure is the FGA construction of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` as an
31	abelian variety with its Albanese universal property.
32	
33	The file contains:
34	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
35	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
36	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
37	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
38	- `picardJacobianWitness`: the Albanese witness `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}`, body `sorry`.
39	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
40	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
41	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
42	  Albanese witness.
43	
44	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
45	
46	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
47	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
48	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
49	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
50	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
51	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`

174	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
175	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
176	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
177	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
178	
179	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
180	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
181	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
182	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
183	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke
184	rigidity / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery — has been
185	removed in favour of this single uniform witness. -/
186	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
187	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
188	    JacobianWitness C :=
189	  sorry
190	
191	/-- Existence of an Albanese witness for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible
192	curve, uniformly in the genus via the Picard identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
193	(`picardJacobianWitness`). This packages all five protected sorries (`Jacobian`,
194	`instGrpObj`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`, `instIsProper`,
195	`instGeometricallyIrreducible`) into a single existence statement, and records that the
196	Albanese property of the underlying scheme `J` is uniform over every choice of
197	`k`-rational marked point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C` (via the `isAlbaneseFor` field of
198	`JacobianWitness`). -/
199	theorem nonempty_jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
200	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
201	    Nonempty (JacobianWitness C) :=
202	  ⟨picardJacobianWitness C⟩
203	
204	/-- A choice of Albanese witness for `C`, extracted via `Classical.choice`.
205	Used to define `Jacobian C` and to discharge each of the four protected instances
206	on it. -/
207	noncomputable def jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
208	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
209	    JacobianWitness C :=
210	  Classical.choice (nonempty_jacobianWitness C)
211	
212	-- data
213	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`.
214	
215	The Jacobian is the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness for `C` (see
216	`JacobianWitness` and `nonempty_jacobianWitness`); the existence of such a
217	witness (`picardJacobianWitness`, `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}`) is the single open
218	mathematical sorry, closed by the FGA construction. The genus-`0`
219	specialisation is implicit in the witness — a smooth proper geometrically
220	irreducible group scheme over `k` of relative dimension `0` is `Spec k` — so
221	no separate genus-`0` construction is needed. -/
222	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
223	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
224	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
225	  (jacobianWitness C).J
226	
227	namespace Jacobian
228	
229	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
230	
231	-- data
232	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
233	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
234	
235	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
236	genus of `C`. -/
237	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
238	  (jacobianWitness C).smoothGenus

240	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
241	instance instIsProper : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom := (jacobianWitness C).proper
242	
243	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
244	instance instGeometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
245	  (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
246

9	/-!
10	# The Abel-Jacobi map
11	
12	The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian, and the universal property
13	of the Jacobian as the Albanese variety.
14	
15	Since `Jacobian C` is by definition `(jacobianWitness C).J`, every declaration below is a
16	projection of the Albanese universal property carried by the witness field
17	`(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P : IsAlbanese C P (jacobianWitness C).J`.
18	
19	## Main results
20	
21	* `Jacobian.ofCurve`: the Abel-Jacobi map `C ⟶ Jacobian C` attached to a `k`-rational point
22	  `P` of `C`.
23	* `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve`: the Abel-Jacobi map sends `P` to the neutral element of
24	  `Jacobian C`.
25	* `Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`: a morphism `f : C ⟶ A` to an abelian variety with
26	  `P ≫ f = η[A]` factors uniquely through the Abel-Jacobi map.
27	
28	## Remaining obligations
29	
30	The genus-0 rigidity input (classical rigidity `Hom(ℙ¹, A) = A(k)`) is not proved here: it is
31	part of the existence claim `nonempty_jacobianWitness` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian`, which is
32	still open.  The `isAlbaneseFor` field of a witness must verify the Albanese property for
33	genus-0 curves too, which is exactly that rigidity content.
34	
35	## References
36	
37	Source: [Mumford], *Abelian Varieties*, §4 (rigidity).
38	-/
39	
40	set_option autoImplicit false
41	
42	universe u
43	
44	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
49	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
50	  [IsProper C.hom]
51	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
52	
53	namespace Jacobian
54	
55	variable {C} in
56	-- data
57	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
58	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. Projects the Albanese universal morphism carried
59	by the witness `(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P`. -/
60	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C := by
61	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
62	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).proper
63	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).smooth
64	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
65	  exact ((jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P).ofCurve
66	
67	variable {C} in
68	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η` below) is
69	the neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. Projects the pointed-property
70	of the Albanese witness `(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P`. -/
71	lemma comp_ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
72	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] := by
73	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
74	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).proper
75	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).smooth
76	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
77	  exact ((jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P).comp_ofCurve
78	
79	variable {C} in
80	/--
81	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`,
82	any morphism `f : C ⟶ A` such that `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the
83	Jacobian of `C`.
84	In other words, `Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
85	
86	The existence-and-uniqueness data is projected unconditionally from the witness
87	`(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P`. The genus-0 rigidity content (`Hom(ℙ¹, A) = A(k)`,
88	Mumford §4) is absorbed into the deferred existence claim `nonempty_jacobianWitness`,
89	since the witness must verify the Albanese property for genus-0 curves too.
90	-/
91	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
92	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
93	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
94	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g := by
95	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
96	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).proper
97	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).smooth
98	  letI := (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
99	  exact ((jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P).exists_unique_ofCurve_comp f hf
100	
101	end Jacobian
102	
103	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	
10	/-!
11	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
12	
13	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
14	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
15	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
16	
17	The relative Picard functor is
18	
19	```
20	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
21	```
22	
23	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
24	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
25	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
26	against it is a natural bijection
27	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
28	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
29	
30	## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5
31	
32	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
33	Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
34	schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
35	`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
36	for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps
37	
38	```
39	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
40	```
41	
42	are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
43	(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
44	itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
45	— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is not
46	representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
47	representability is asserted only **conditionally on `[HasRationalPoint C]`**:
48	an unconditional statement would be false. For the same reason `picSharp` may
49	not be wired to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.
50	
51	## Main results
52	
53	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
54	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
55	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
56	  quotient encoding).
57	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
58	  scheme and the natural bijection
59	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
60	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
61	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
62	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
63	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
64	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
65	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
66	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
67	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
68	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
69	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
70	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
71	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
72	
73	## Remaining obligations
74	
75	One statement in this file is still `sorry`: `instHasPicScheme`, the existence
76	of a scheme that represents `picSharp C` and is separated and locally of
77	finite type over `k`, given a rational point. Mathematically this is Kleiman
78	§4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`, transported through §2
79	Thm 2.5. Everything else here — in particular representability of the chosen
80	scheme, its local finiteness, its separatedness, and its group-scheme
81	structure — is derived from that one existence statement.
82	
83	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
84	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
85	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
86	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
87	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
88	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
89	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
90	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
91	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
92	
93	## References
94	
95	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
96	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
97	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
98	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
99	-/
100

108	
109	namespace Scheme
110	
111	/-- **`C` has a `k`-rational point**: the structural morphism `C.hom` admits a
112	section `σ : Spec k ⟶ C.left`. For the smooth proper geometrically integral
113	curves of this project this is the pointing `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ C`
114	already threaded through the Albanese statements (`AlgebraicJacobian.IsAlbanese`).
115	
116	This is the hypothesis of Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: together with
117	`O_S = f_* O_X` universally (automatic for proper geometrically integral
118	fibers), a section forces the comparison maps
119	`Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)` to be bijective, so
120	the *plain* relative Picard functor is already the étale sheaf that FGA
121	representability (Kleiman §4) represents. -/
122	class HasRationalPoint {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Prop where
123	  nonempty_section :
124	    Nonempty {σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left // σ ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))}

132	structure forgotten (representability is a statement about the underlying
133	set-valued functor; the group structure is transported back onto the
134	representing scheme by `groupSchemeStructure` below).
135	
136	`divFunctor` (the relative-effective-divisor functor `Div_{C/k}`, Kleiman §3
137	Def `df:div`) is the functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of sibling
138	`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`. -/
139	
140	/-- **The relative Picard functor** `Pic^♯_{C/k} : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)`,
141	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` — the set-valued shadow of the group-valued
142	presheaf `PicSharp.relPresheaf` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (the honest
143	`H_T`-coset carrier of Kleiman §2 Def `df:Pfs`).
144	
145	Universe note: the values live in `Type (u+1)` because the line-bundle
146	carrier `LineBundle.OnProduct` is a quotient of (large) sheaves of modules.
147	`Functor.RepresentableBy` is universe-polymorphic, so representability by a
148	(`Type u`-homed) scheme remains a well-formed — and, under a rational point,
149	true — statement. -/
150	noncomputable def picSharp {k : Type u} [Field k]
151	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
152	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
153	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
154	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
155	
156	/-- Typeclass asserting existence of the relative-divisor functor `Div_{C/k}`.
157	The instance `instHasDivFunctor` below discharges it, with witness
158	`divFunctor C = DivFunctor C.hom`; the class survives as the blueprint-pinned
159	existence carrier (`def:has_div_functor`).
160	
161	**Vacuity warning.** The field
162	`has_div_functor : Nonempty ((Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1))` does not
163	mention `C` at all: any functor (e.g. a constant functor) witnesses it, so
164	the class is vacuously true and carries no mathematical content. It must
165	never be cited as evidence that the relative-divisor functor of `C` exists —
166	use `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) directly, as
167	`divFunctor` below does. -/
168	class HasDivFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Prop where
169	  has_div_functor : Nonempty ((Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1))
170	
171	/-- **The relative-divisor functor** `Div_{C/k} : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)`,
172	sending a `k`-scheme `T` to the set of relative effective Cartier divisors on
173	`C ×_k T` flat over `T` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`).
174	
175	It is defined as
176	
177	```
178	divFunctor C := Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom
179	```
180	
181	with `Scheme.DivFunctor` from sibling `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`: `T`-flat
182	invertible-kernel quotients of `O_{C ×_k T}` modulo `ker q = ker q'`, i.e.
183	Kleiman's set of relative effective divisors. The definition does not route
184	through the `HasDivFunctor` carrier class above. -/
185	noncomputable def divFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k]
186	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
187	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
188	  DivFunctor C.hom
189	
190	/-- Existence instance for `HasDivFunctor`: the relative-divisor functor
191	`divFunctor C = Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` witnesses the existential. -/
192	instance instHasDivFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k]
193	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) : HasDivFunctor C :=
194	  ⟨⟨divFunctor C⟩⟩
195	
196	end PicScheme
197	
198	/-! ## §1. The Picard scheme
199	
200	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` of a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
201	`C/k` **with a `k`-rational point** is the `k`-scheme representing the
202	relative Picard functor `picSharp C` (which, under the rational point, agrees
203	with the étale-sheafified functor of Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` by Kleiman §2
204	Thm 2.5). The scheme is separated, locally of finite type over `k`, and a
205	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes; the
206	abelian-group-scheme structure is `groupSchemeStructure` below.
207	
208	Blueprint reference: `def:pic_scheme` (Kleiman §4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/
209	
210	/-- Typeclass asserting existence of a scheme over `Spec k` that represents
211	the relative Picard functor `picSharp C` and is **separated and locally of
212	finite type over `k`**. The instance below is the file's only `sorry`, and it
213	is **conditional on `[HasRationalPoint C]`** — without a section the plain
214	relative functor is not representable in general, so an unconditional instance
215	would assert a false statement. Consumers that quantify over `[HasPicScheme
216	C]` as a hypothesis remain kernel-clean.

268	
269	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
270	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
271	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
272	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.

277	/-! ### The Abel map
278	
279	The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
280	`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
281	supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.
282	
283	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
284	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
285	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
286	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
287	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
288	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
289	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
290	negation on the group-valued functor.
291	
292	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
293	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
294	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
295	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
296	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
297	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
298	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
299	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
300

300	
301	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
302	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
303	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
304	naturality rest only on the kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
305	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
306	
307	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
308	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
309	representability (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`) is NOT claimed here. -/

312	divisor equivalence relation `DivFamily.Rel`: an equivalence `f : x.F ≅ y.F`
313	with `x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q` gives `ker x.q ≅ ker y.q` (`kernelCompMono` at the
314	iso `f.hom`), hence equal `H_T`-coset classes (`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/

316	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) {x y : DivFamily C.hom T.unop} (h : x.Rel y) :
317	    Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
318	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) =

345	      x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
346	  exact kernelIsIsoComp

348	        (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf)).inv
349	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).map x.q) ≪≫

358	noncomputable def abelKernelNatTrans {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

366	  naturality {T T'} g := by
367	    ext a
368	    induction a using Quotient.ind with | _ x => ?_
369	    apply Quotient.sound
370	    apply PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
371	    exact ⟨abelKernelBaseChangeIso C g x⟩

454	
455	The structural lemma underlying Step 4 of Kleiman §4 Thm. `th:main`: given a
456	surjection `α : Z ⟶ P` of étale sheaves with `R := Z ×_P Z` representable,
457	`Z` representable **by a quasi-projective scheme**, and the first projection
458	`R ⟶ Z` smooth and proper, the quotient `P` is representable.
459	
460	The hypothesis list expressible here is strictly weaker than Kleiman §4 Lem
461	`lm:qt`: it lacks **quasi-projectivity of `Y`**, for which Mathlib has no
462	vocabulary at the pinned revision. Without it the statement is false: a
463	Hironaka-type free `ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold
464	gives a smooth proper equivalence relation satisfying hypotheses (1)–(4)
465	whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is not a scheme. In
466	particular there is no global instance of `HasSmoothProperQuotient`; such an
467	instance would assert that every presheaf receiving any natural
468	transformation is representable.
469	
470	`HasSmoothProperQuotient α` is therefore an **explicit use-site hypothesis**:
471	the intended consumer (the FGA assembly, Step 4 of `th:main`) instantiates it
472	for the Abel-map slice `Z ⟶ P^{φ_0}_0`, where `Z` is a quasi-projective open
473	of `Div_{C/k}` and Altman–Kleiman descent genuinely applies. Supplying that
474	instance is part of the `instHasPicScheme` obligation, not a standalone
475	global fact.
476

484	false statement (see the section header). The class is supplied at the use

599	multiplicative). Carrier-level it is the same functor: `Multiplicative` is a
600	type synonym. -/
601	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
602	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
603	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
604	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
605	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp
606	
607	/-- The set-valued shadows of `picSharpCommGrp` and `picSharp` agree up to
608	the canonical `Multiplicative.ofAdd` bijection (a natural isomorphism, since
609	`Multiplicative` is carrier-preserving). -/
610	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrpForgetIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
611	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
612	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
613	    picSharp C ≅ picSharpCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
614	  NatIso.ofComponents
615	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd
616	      (α := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type (u+1)))))
617	    (fun _ => rfl)
618	
619	/-- **The Picard scheme is a commutative `k`-group scheme** — a canonical
620	`CommGrpObj` structure (i.e. `GrpObj` + `IsCommMonObj`) on `PicScheme C`,
621	obtained by Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the
622	abelian-group structure of the relative Picard presheaf
623	`PicSharp.relPresheaf` along the representability witness `representable C`.
624	Concretely: `[L] + [M] = [L ⊗ M]`, `-[L] = [L⁻¹]`, unit `[O_{C ×_k T}]`,
625	transported through `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`.
626	
627	Commutativity comes for free from the transport, so this is the full
628	abelian-group-scheme statement of the blueprint
629	(`thm:pic_is_group_scheme`). -/
630	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructure {k : Type u} [Field k]
631	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
632	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
633	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
634	    CommGrpObj (PicScheme C) :=
635	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicScheme C) (picSharpCommGrp C)
636	    ((representable C).ofIso (picSharpCommGrpForgetIso C))
637	
638	/-! ## §6. Local finiteness of the Picard scheme
639	
640	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): the Picard scheme is separated and locally of
641	finite type over the base. `HasPicScheme` packages local finiteness together
642	with the representability existential (one existence package, as in Kleiman's
643	theorem), so the carrier below is obtained by extraction. It is what the
644	identity-component substrate (`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`,
645	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent`) consumes to specialise to
646	`G = PicScheme C`. -/
647	
648	/-- Typeclass asserting that the structural morphism of the Picard scheme is
649	locally of finite type (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): `Pic_{C/k}` is a
650	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes, hence locally of
651	finite type). The `HasPicScheme` existential carries local finiteness, so the
652	property of the `Classical.choose` witness is its second `choose_spec`
653	component; the class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer
654	signature. -/
655	class PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
656	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
657	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
658	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
659	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme C).hom
660	
661	/-- Existence instance for `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`: Kleiman §4 Thm
662	`th:main`(1) makes local finiteness part of the same existence package as
663	representability, so the `HasPicScheme` existential carries it and the
664	property of the chosen witness is the second component of its `choose_spec`.
665	The instance hypothesis is `[HasPicScheme C]` rather than
666	`[HasRationalPoint C]`: the rational-point conditionality lives entirely in
667	`instHasPicScheme` (which supplies `HasPicScheme C`), and any consumer able
668	to name `PicScheme C` already quantifies over `[HasPicScheme C]`. -/
669	instance instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
670	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
671	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
672	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
673	    PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C :=
674	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.2.1⟩

678	C).hom` whenever the carrier class is in scope (as the identity-component

681	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
682	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
683	    [PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
684	    LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme C).hom :=
685	  PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType.locallyOfFiniteType
686	
687	/-- **`Pic_{C/k}` is separated over `k`.**
688	
689	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` packages separatedness together with representability

/-! ## §1. The Picard scheme

The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` of a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
`C/k` **with a `k`-rational point** is the `k`-scheme representing the
relative Picard functor `picSharp C` (which, under the rational point, agrees
with the étale-sheafified functor of Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` by Kleiman §2
Thm 2.5). The scheme is separated, locally of finite type over `k`, and a
disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes; the
abelian-group-scheme structure is `groupSchemeStructure` below.

Blueprint reference: `def:pic_scheme` (Kleiman §4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/

/-- Typeclass asserting existence of a scheme over `Spec k` that represents
the relative Picard functor `picSharp C` and is **separated and locally of
finite type over `k`**. The instance below is the file's only `sorry`, and it
is **conditional on `[HasRationalPoint C]`** — without a section the plain
relative functor is not representable in general, so an unconditional instance
would assert a false statement. Consumers that quantify over `[HasPicScheme
C]` as a hypothesis remain kernel-clean.

Representability, local finiteness and separatedness are bundled into a single
existential because Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) delivers them as one package:
`Pic_{C/k}` is a separated scheme locally of finite type over `k`, a disjoint
union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes. Bundling therefore adds no
strength beyond representability, and lets the carriers
`PicScheme.instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` and `PicScheme.isSeparated` be
obtained by extraction. -/
class HasPicScheme {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
  has_pic_scheme : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
    Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom

/-- The **Picard scheme** `Pic_{C/k}` of a smooth proper geometrically
integral curve `C/k`, encoded as an object of `Over (Spec (.of k))`.

Extracted (`Classical.choose`) from the `HasPicScheme` existence field, so it
carries the identity "this scheme represents the relative Picard functor
`picSharp C`" through `representable` below — a natural bijection onto
`Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`. -/
noncomputable def PicScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  (HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose

/-- Existence instance for `HasPicScheme` — the **one unproved statement of
this file**. Mathematical content: Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` + Cor
`cor:algsch` (the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor of a smooth proper
geometrically integral curve is representable by a separated `k`-scheme
locally of finite type, a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
`k`-subschemes), combined with Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (under the `k`-rational
point of `[HasRationalPoint C]`, the plain relative functor `picSharp C`
coincides with the étale-sheafified one, so the same scheme represents it).
All three conjuncts of the existential — representability, local finiteness,
separatedness — are parts of that one Kleiman theorem.

The conditionality on `[HasRationalPoint C]` is essential for truth: without
a section, `Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` need not even be a Zariski sheaf. -/
noncomputable instance instHasPicScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasRationalPoint C] : HasPicScheme C :=
  ⟨sorry⟩

561	      SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{0} (Fin r)))

571	implicit locality behind the chart construction).  Families of rank-`d`
572	locally free quotients glue along an open cover of the parameter scheme:
573	the target sheaves glue by descent of sheaves of modules along the cover
574	(the `Scheme.Modules.glue` engine of `GlueDescent.lean` at the glue datum of
575	the cover), the quotient maps glue through the descent-equalizer lift

###### RigidPushforward.lean (738)
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
-/
import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.HilbertPolynomial
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.LineBundlePullback
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatteningStratification
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GlueDescent
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietorisCover
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FlatBaseChange
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.FinitenessP1

/-!
# B3 — the rigid pushforward engine: statement layer and ℙ¹ reduction skeleton

This file pins milestone **B3** of the Picard-representability campaign
(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), the engine
`pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing`: for the constant curve
`C_A = C ×_k Spec A` over a finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` and an
invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A` with `h¹(C_t, L_t) = 0` at **every scheme
point** `t : Spec A`, the pushforward `q_* L` along `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is
locally free with fibre rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t) (= χ(L_t))`, and its formation
commutes with **arbitrary** ring maps `A → A'`.

Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 (the two-term finite free
complex and "cohomology and base change"); EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5 — B3 is the engine
behind Kleiman's flattening/openness arguments in the curve case.

## Statement audit (campaign checklist item 1 — BLOCKING; verdicts recorded here)

* **Quantifier — `h¹ = 0` at ALL scheme points** (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`,
  `RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): the hypothesis `∀ t : Spec A,
  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points
  only.  A finitely generated `k`-algebra *is* Jacobson, so on the pinned
  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper
  semicontinuity, an engine we refuse to smuggle into the *statement*, and
  (ii) milestone B2 extends every consumer along filtered colimits and
  localizations, where the base is merely noetherian and Jacobson genuinely
  fails.  All campaign consumers (J1/J3 `h⁰ ≡ 1`, B4–B6) supply the
  hypothesis at all scheme points anyway.  VERDICT: pin at all scheme points.
* **Base change along ARBITRARY `A → A'` in the statement**
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): quantified over every commutative ring
  `A' : Type u` and every ring hom `φ : A →+* A'` — no finiteness, no
  flatness, no noetherian hypothesis on `A'`.  The comparison morphism is
  the canonical `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` (Stacks 02N4-style mate) of the
  *defining pullback square* of `q` along `Spec φ`, so the statement is
  well-formed with zero transport: the base-changed family is
  `pullback q (Spec.map φ)` — canonically (but not definitionally) isomorphic
  to `C ×_k Spec A'`; the comparison iso is postponed to the consumer layer
  (B2), keeping the pin transport-free.  VERDICT: arbitrary `A'`, arbitrary
  `φ`, canonical square, comparison map in the statement.
* **Two-step pin**: step 1 = rank-`χ` local freeness
  (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`) + base change
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`); step 2 = the rank-one corollary
  (`pushforward_isLocallyTrivial_of_h1_vanishing`, proved from the gate).
  VERDICT: pinned as two separate `Prop`s consumed by one gate.
* **Rank = `χ(L_t)`** : under `h¹(L_t) = 0` we have `χ(L_t) = h⁰(L_t)`, and
  `h⁰` *is* expressible today (`Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`, the `κ(t)`-dimension of
  `Γ(C_t, L_t)`, matching `Scheme.hilbertFunction`'s convention), while the
  `χ`-ledger is milestone P3.  The rank is therefore pinned as
  `q.fiberH0 L t`; **P2/P3-interface TODO**: once the P2 cohomology kit and
  the P3 `χ`-ledger land, add the (definitionally compatible) reformulation
  `rank = χ(L_t) = deg L_t + 1 - g`.
* **Fibrewise `h¹` vocabulary** (P2 does not exist yet): the hypothesis is
  pinned in the weakest honest form the adelic lane can already express —
  existence of a 2-affine Čech cover (`AffineCoverMVSquare`, the lane's
  carrier) of the scheme-theoretic fibre on which the degree-1 Čech
  cokernel of `L_t` vanishes, i.e. the difference-of-restrictions map is
  surjective (`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing`; carrier form
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok`, mirroring
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok` of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`).  On a
  separated scheme with an affine 2-cover, this Čech `H¹` computes sheaf
  `H¹` for quasi-coherent modules (Mayer–Vietoris/Leray; in-lane precedent
  `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`), and any two such covers agree —
  cover-independence is exactly the **P2-interface TODO**, to be discharged
  Čech-to-Čech.  The ∃-form is chosen because it is *implied* by every
  future kit form, so the gate only gets easier to discharge.
* **The rank-one corollary's `DivFamily` leg** (Kleiman §5; campaign J2):
  `h⁰ ≡ 1, h¹ ≡ 0 ⟹ q_*L` invertible is pinned and proved from the gate
  below.  The continuation — the counit section `q^*q_*L ⟶ L` is fibrewise
  nonzero, hence a regular section on the integral fibres, hence cuts a
  canonical `DivFamily` — needs the counit/adjunction vocabulary on the
  `Div` side and the geometric integrality of fibres; it is recorded as the
  **J2-interface TODO** and deliberately NOT pinned here (its natural home
  is the J2 session, where the target `DivFamily` shape is fixed).

## Gate

`HasRigidPushforward C` is the campaign gate (`HasPicScheme` pattern): a
`Prop` class with **no instances anywhere**, carrying the two statement
`Prop`s quantified over all finitely generated `k`-algebras.  It is
discharged by the full B3 session (Mumford two-term complex route) and
deleted on discharge.  Everything else in this file is *proved*: the
extraction theorems, the rank-one corollary, and the ℙ¹ reduction skeleton
(the base-changed finite map `C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A`, the pushforward factorization
`q_* = p_* ∘ π_*`, and the reduction of B3-for-`C_A` to a ℙ¹ engine plus a
named finite-pushforward transfer package).
-/

/-!
# B3 transfer package — discharging the named hypotheses of the ℙ¹ reduction

`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` reduces B3 local freeness for the constant
curve `C_A` to the ℙ¹ engine plus a *finite-pushforward transfer package*
along the finite map `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` (`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`,
hypotheses `hfp`/`hflat`/`hH1`/`hH0`).  This file discharges the first two
transfer hypotheses:

* **`hfp` (Stacks 01XZ/087T flavour)** —
  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_isFinitePresentation`: the finite
  pushforward `(π_A)_* L` of an invertible module is finitely presented.
  The engine behind it is the general noetherian coherence criterion
  `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`: a quasi-coherent
  module on a locally noetherian scheme whose section modules over affine
  opens are finite is finitely presented.  The pushforward is quasi-coherent
  by Stacks 01XJ (`pushforward_isQuasicoherent`, proved in
  `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), its sections over an affine `V` are
  `Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` *definitionally*, and these are module-finite over
  `Γ(ℙ¹_A, V)` by composing the module-finiteness of the finite morphism
  `π_A` (Stacks 01WG) with the finiteness of the sections of the finitely
  presented `L` on the affine `π_A⁻¹ V` (Stacks 01PC,
  `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`).  `A` is a finitely generated
  `k`-algebra, hence noetherian (Hilbert basis), hence `ℙ¹_A` is locally
  noetherian and finite section modules are finitely presented.

* **`hflat` (mixed-base flat stability)** —
  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_coherentSheafFlat`: `(π_A)_* L`
  stays `CoherentSheafFlat` over `Spec A`.  Since
  `Γ((π_A)_* L, V) = Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` definitionally and
  `q = π_A ≫ p` (`finiteMapToP1BaseChange_snd`), the statement reduces to
  `CoherentSheafFlat q L` for the invertible `L` on the `A`-flat family
  `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` (`coherentSheafFlat_pushforward_of_isAffineHom`).
  The latter is `coherentSheafFlat_of_isLocallyTrivial_of_flat`: on a
  trivialising affine chart `W` the section module `Γ(L, W)` is an
  invertible (hence flat) `Γ(C_A, W)`-module
  (`isInvertible_of_restrict_iso`), `Γ(C_A, W)` is flat over `A` because
  `q` is a flat morphism (base change of `C ⟶ Spec k`, and everything over
  the one-point integral `Spec k` is flat), and chart flatness globalises
  to all affine pairs by the affine-locality engine
  `flat_section_of_affine_cover` (`Picard/GenericFlatnessGeometric.lean`).

* **transfer item (c) — the fibre-compatibility isomorphism and `hH0`**
  (§6–§7): the general Stacks 02KG (`i = 0`) engine for **affine**
  morphisms and **arbitrary** (non-flat) base change
  (`isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback`), its fibre specialization
  `fiberPushforwardCompatIso : (p.fiberι t)^* ((π_A)_* L) ≅ (π_t)_* (L_t)`,
  the verbatim `hH0` discharge
  (`pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fiberH0`), and the `hH1` transfer
  reduced to Čech cover-independence of `Ȟ¹`-vanishing on the fibre curve
  (`fiberH1Vanishing_pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_of_coverIndependence`).

* **`hH1`** — the cover-independence obligation `hindep` is
  discharged by the QC-vanishing keystone
  (`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/QuasicoherentDegreeOneVanishing.lean`:
  degree-1 affine vanishing for quasi-coherent modules + the Mayer–Vietoris
  `(0,1)`-slice on every 2-affine cover), giving the verbatim pinned `hH1`
  (`pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_fiberH1`).  All four transfer
  hypotheses being discharged, B3 local freeness for `C_A` follows from the
  ℙ¹ engine alone (`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1Engine`).

No pinned statement is touched: this file only *produces* the named
hypotheses consumed by `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`.

Sources: Stacks 01XJ (pushforward quasi-coherence), 01XZ/087T (finite
pushforward of coherent is coherent), 01PC (finite sections on affines),
01WG (finite morphisms are module-finite on affines), 00HB/00HT (flatness
is affine-local), 02KG (cohomology and base change, `i = 0`); Nitsure §4;
Mumford AV II §5.
-/

The elementary bookkeeping lemma for moving `Module.Finite` across the
section comparisons of the fromSpec dictionary: a surjective-semilinear
additive equivalence transports finite generation. -/

equivalence.**  If `e : M ≃+ N` intertwines the `R`-action on `M` with the

finite `R`-module: the preimages of a finite `S`-generating set generate
`M` over `R`, because every `S`-scalar lifts along `σ`. -/
